reviews.quote: High-end convertible now with a larger 120-Hz OLED — the Spectre x360 14 remains a benchmark premium 2-in-1.
A near-perfect 2-in-1 worthy of your money — impressive battery life and a gorgeous OLED display; you'll forget about its minor flaws real quick.

praises: Gorgeous 2.8K OLED 120Hz touch — the best panel HP ever put in this chassis
Gem-cut aluminum build with the tightest hinge of any HP convertible
Thunderbolt 4 x2 + microSD slot: better media/dock story than the OmniBook successors
5MP webcam with physical shutter is still class-leading for calls
32GB/2TB spec at full tilt — maxed-out configuration of the line
complaints: BBY clearance unit rated 2.0/5 by 3 buyers (small sample) — battery degradation and returns cited on leftover stock
Meteor Lake H runs warm and fan-assertive in this thin convertible
Battery life mediocre (~9h) vs the 11h+ OmniBook X Flip successors
No discount at $2,399.97 when the newer OLED OmniBook sells for $2,179
Line is discontinued: future spare parts/warranty support will thin out

design_philosophy: The final Spectre x360 14 was HP's flagship convertible before the OmniBook rebrand: jewel-like gem-cut aluminum, a 120Hz 2.8K OLED, and the best port/pen/webcam package HP has shipped in a 14-inch 2-in-1. This maxed 32GB/2TB leftover is a legacy buy — superb hardware, but clearance pricing and mixed late-stock experiences blunt the appeal.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from the widely-reviewed 2024 Spectre x360 14 line (OLED 120Hz, 68Wh, ~1.44 kg) with the max RAM/storage tier; Meteor Lake H deltas (-battery, +heat) applied vs successors. No numeric pro score re-fetched this session (NBC/PCMag bot-walls — see SHARED-hp-convertibles.md); BBY user sample tiny (2.0★/3). Included as discontinued-legacy entry per task instruction to check Spectre availability.
standouts: Best panel + build in the whole HP convertible family
dealbreakers: Discontinued line at full clearance price
